items.reason: test_tenacity.py::TestStopConditions.test_stop_after_attempt asserts `self.assertTrue(r.stop(make_retry_state(3, 6546)))`, where r.stop IS the stop_after_attempt(3) instance (Retrying.__init__ sets self.stop=stop) and make_retry_state(3, ...) sets attempt_number=3 — an exact assertion at the changed boundary that the >=->> flip breaks (3 >= 3 is True; 3 > 3 is False). The change IS discriminated, so ripr should have read exposed and stayed quiet. Instead it read weakly_exposed/orthogonal and routed a repair card: a FALSE_ACTIONABLE. Root cause: syntactic sink-alignment cannot trace the local binding r.stop -> stop_after_attempt.__call__ nor the factory make_retry_state(3, ...) -> attempt_number; the oracle text contains no owner or changed-sink token. This is the documented __call__-via-local-instance limitation (#1172). Conservative direction: over-suggest, never over-credit.

No click test references the internal helper _is_compat_stream_attr (it is called only by _is_jupyter_kernel_output); no discriminating oracle reaches the changed predicate. ripr's no_static_path is honest — a true gap, neither over-credited (false_exposed=false) nor over-suggested (false_actionable=false; no_static_path routes an add-a-test gap, appropriate when no test exists). Correct conservative judgment.

The change sits in a module-init class-body version conditional (sys.version_info[1] <= 1) inside _MovedItems — legacy Python 3.0/3.1 gating that is effectively dead and untestable on modern Python. ripr fails closed to static_unknown, which is honest (no over-credit past the limit: false_exposed=false; no card: false_actionable=false). limitation_quality=imprecise: no_static_path would arguably describe it more precisely than a static-analysis limit, but failing closed is the safe call.
